_readme: One file per tenant; results are never pooled across tenants, because each
has a different corpus and a different 60-day window.
Each case names a topic_label the pipeline has actually produced (match it
exactly; comparison is case-insensitive) and the ground truth for it:
ongoing     - you can point at earlier coverage of this topic in this
tenant's corpus, from before the analysis window.
new         - genuinely new in this window. Nothing earlier covers it.
adversarial - invented. It cannot have prior coverage, because it never
happened. Calling one of these 'ongoing' fails the gate
outright, no matter the precision figure.
All three labels must be present or the gate measures nothing. Aim for at
least 40 ongoing, 40 new, and 20 adversarial per tenant, so that 100
Adversarial cases have to be run through detection to get a shadow decision.
The practical route is to add them as themes on a scratch topic filter, or
to replay them with the same code path the pipeline uses.
